item.title: Soldier blasts Bennett over Madma memorial demolition

item.title: “Now I’m calm:" Footage of rescue of Israeli who accidentally entered Ramallah
item.description: A Holon resident mistakenly entered Area A in the Ramallah area and contacted the police emergency hotline. Border Police officers located his vehicle and quickly rescued him unharmed.

item.title: The price of terror stipends: Major raid on homes of released terrorists
item.description: Security forces raided properties belonging to released terrorists who received salaries from the Palestinian Authority, seizing vehicles and tens of thousands of shekels.

item.title: Givati soldiers punished after refusing to ride with female medic
item.description: Three Givati soldiers reportedly refused to board a Namer carrying a female medic, citing rabbinic instructions. All soldiers in their platoon were sentenced to 21 days of confinement.

item.title: Fatal chase: Car thief killed trying to flee Jerusalem police
item.description: A vehicle theft in Jerusalem ended overnight Wednesday with the death of the suspected thief and the light wounding of a police officer and a civilian.

item.title: IDF revolutionizes its mehadrin kosher food
item.description: Instead of prepared meals for reheating, soldiers will receive fresh, varied Mehadrin kosher food that meets stringent halachic standards.

item.title: Report: Yair Netanyahu was target of Iranian assassination attempt
item.description:
Prime Minister Netanyahu's son Yair was reportedly the target of the Iranian assassination plot that was revealed this week and was forced to leave for Israel as soon as the plot was uncovered.
Read more

item.title: Italy proposes UNIFIL alternative
item.description:
Lebanese media reported that Italy has proposed to establish a smaller multinational force, with UN approval, to replace UNIFIL in southern Lebanon. According to the outline, the force will focus on supporting the Lebanese army, protecting the civilian population, assisting the US-led ceasefire mechanism, and future disarmament arrangements, as well as monitoring violations and reducing escalation between Israel and Lebanon.
According to the report in Nidaa al-Watan, the success of the plan depends on resolving a number of issues that have not yet been resolved, including the command structure, the scope of the forces, the rules of engagement, the funding, the verification powers in the pilot areas, and the possibility of reactivating the ceasefire mechanism that has been suspended since March.

item.title: Thief killed fleeing police in Jerusalem car chase
item.description:
A suspect in a car theft from the Katamon neighborhood in Jerusalem was killed after fleeing the police, driving against traffic and colliding with a pillar and a private vehicle at the A-Tur junction.
According to the police, during the chase the officers fired at the vehicle's wheels in an attempt to stop it. A policeman and a civilian were lightly injured. The suspect was evacuated to the hospital in critical condition while undergoing resuscitation but was later pronounced dead.

item.title: US halts all visa applications
item.description: All US visa applications have been suspended by the Trump administration in an effort to combat immigration and prevent the entry of immigrants who “will require public assistance."

item.title: Ukraine strikes Russian retail giant
item.description:
Ukrainian media reported that Ukrainian drones hit a logistics complex of the Russian retail giant Wildberries in the Tambov region.
The company's facilities in the region have been hit in previous Ukrainian strikes.

item.title: The fifth 'language of Redemption'
item.description: There are four languages of the redemption promised by Hashem, - for which, the four glasses of wine are drunk at the Seder - but there is a fifth promise as well. Which promise is that?

item.title: Man arrested for bringing guillotine to Capitol Hill
item.description:
Capitol Police in Washington, D.C., arrested a 35-year-old man from California after a guillotine was found in the bed of his pickup truck. Police said the truck was illegally parked near the Capitol complex.
According to authorities, the man was traveling from California to Washington, and investigators are looking into why he came to the city and what he intened to do with the guillotine. He was arrested on suspicion of possessing a dangerous weapon.

item.title: Telling G-d what to do
item.description: We are not the givers, but are merely transferring what Hashem has allotted. Happy is the one who has the merit to serve as Hashem’s delivery person.

item.title: Gratitude has a memory
item.description: The farmer does not simply bring his fruit to Jerusalem. He tells a story.

item.title: US freezes visa appointments worldwide
item.description:
The administration has ordered a temporary freeze on visa appointments at American embassies and consulates around the world. The State Department said the move was intended to allow for a global training program for consular officers, in order to improve screening and ensure a uniform examination of visa applicants, among other things, regarding the possibility that they would be dependent on public assistance in the United States.
According to the Financial Times, visa applicants who had already been scheduled for interviews received notices of postponed appointments, and were informed that a new date would be set in due course. At this time, no timetable for the resumption of appointments has been announced.

item.title: Rom Braslavski: “I was afraid, but I didn’t hesitate"
item.description: Captivity survivor Rom Braslavski recounted the moment in captivity when he was forced to reveal his identity as a soldier - about six months after the murderous attack. “I realize I’m done for."

item.title: Iran Regime Change: Why it has failed and what must happen now
item.description: The dilemma facing Washington and Jerusalem: A nuclear-capable Iran that still funds proxies from Lebanon to Yemen is not a foreign-policy result. It is a failure. What can the US do? Opinion.

item.title: Report: Ukrainian drones hit a Wildbreeze logistics complex in Russia
item.description:
Ukrainian media reported that Ukrainian drones hit a logistics complex of the Russian retail giant WildBreeze in the Tambov region.
The company's facilities in the province have already been damaged in previous attacks by Ukraine.

item.title: US temporarily freezes visa appointments at embassies worldwide
item.description:
The administration of US President Donald Trump has ordered a temporary freeze on visa appointments at US embassies and consulates around the world. The State Department said the move is intended to allow for a global training program for consular employees, aimed at improving screening and ensuring uniform evaluation of visa applicants, including regarding the possibility that they may become dependent on welfare benefits and public assistance in the United States.
According to the Financial Times, immigrant visa applicants who had already been scheduled for interviews received notices that their appointments had been postponed and were told that a new date would be set at a later time. At this stage, no timetable has been provided for the resumption of appointments.

item.title: Dolly Parton’s representatives: She died after a brief battle with cancer
item.description:
Representatives for country music legend Dolly Parton, who died Tuesday at the age of 80, said she passed away following a “brief battle with cancer." Parton died at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville, surrounded by her family.
The type of cancer she had was not disclosed.
